scope: staged preflight component ONLY; no merge/native/full-issue acceptance

findings.claim: The capability label is the only gate in this staged slice, so the slice is not fail-closed for an adapter that advertises it. Suppose an adapter advertises PreparedInputAdmission in both capabilities() and probe(), with a matching agent and a non-empty provider. It passes preflight and then runs the unchanged legacy path: reserve, ordinary marker persist, adapter.start, and finally the legacy Task-rewriting binding (history[index].session_id = Some(...); self.persist). No #19 private allocation or binder predicate is checked anywhere on that path. No in-tree adapter advertises the capability today, so current behavior is fail-closed. The risk is during co-integration: once #19 preparation lands and a fixture (FakeAgent or Generic) is migrated to advertise the capability before the binder composes, positive tests would go through the very Task rewrite #43 removes and look like coverage. That contradicts 'Staged #43 production fails closed without #19 and earns no positive binding coverage'. None of the six probe cases is fully consistent, so this path has no control.
findings.evidence: preflight_native_adapter returns Ok(NativeAdapterSelection) whenever both capability surfaces and the probe identity agree. prepare_agent then still sets dispatch_started, calls self.persist, calls adapter.start, and on success sets session_id and calls self.persist(&mut snapshot, None). The test spoofs in native_preflight_rejects_contradictory_probe_without_durable_mutation all remove one required element. The mechanics doc says: 'capability alone never certifies those proofs'.
findings.fix: Add an explicit crate-private staged refusal after a successful preflight, before any reservation or context write. It should return a typed 'managed binder/#19 predicate not composed' error and be removed only in the co-integration commit that compiles the real binder. Add a fully consistent spoof case (both surfaces, matching identity) that asserts no durable change and zero launches. Add a mutant that deletes the staged refusal and must be killed. This keeps migrated positive fixtures from earning coverage through legacy binding.

findings.claim: Two of the slice's new guards are never executed, yet the verification lists them as implemented without saying so. First, the returned-Session provider check (session.provider == provider), along with the added worktree clause. Second, the new 'selected adapter changed during preparation' check. Every native positive now stops at preflight, so neither check has a passing control or a killed mutant. Also, the added clause `Some(&session.worktree) == snapshot.task.worktree.as_ref()` is redundant: `worktree` was just cloned from snapshot.task.worktree, and the next condition already compares session.worktree == worktree.
findings.evidence: The mutation artifact lists only the omit-admission, preflight-after-reservation, probe-identity, static-capability and probe-capability mutants. The verification doc lists 'returned provider cross-check' and retained selection among the slice's guards. The legacy actor-override test (preparation_actor_override_uses_new_claim_before_launch_and_binding_is_immutable) cannot reach those checks while the capability is absent.
findings.fix: Label both checks in the verification doc as implemented but causally unverified, pending a genuine #19 positive fixture. When that fixture exists, add controls for a returned provider mismatch and for a change of actor after preflight (with retained-claim assertions), each with a killed mutant. Remove the redundant worktree clause or document why it is kept.

findings.claim: Every native reservation step now calls adapter.probe() synchronously on the async Engine path, before reservation. The old code checked only capabilities() and never probed. AgentAdapter::probe is a synchronous public trait method with no bounded-time or non-blocking contract. GenericCliAdapter's probe does filesystem resolution and canonicalization, and provider probes outside this tree may do more. A slow or blocking probe stalls the tokio worker for the whole step. Probe errors are returned as Err without durable attention, which the design accepts, so callers need bounded retry behavior.
findings.evidence: Code: `let info = adapter.probe()?;` inside the synchronous preflight_native_adapter, which is called from the async step. GenericCliAdapter::probe calls resolve_executable, which reads metadata and canonicalizes the path. The trait doc says nothing about probe latency.
findings.fix: Keep the static capability check first. Then either run probe via spawn_blocking with a bounded deadline, or pin a non-blocking, bounded probe contract in the trait documentation and verify each provider's probe against it during co-integration. Add a control where a slow probe neither blocks unrelated work nor writes durable state.

review.assessment:
This is an observed independent review of public bytes for the staged preflight component only. It makes no private-memory or OS secrecy claim and no whole-#43, native, merge or MVP readiness claim. All producer and co-integration gates stay open and none is waived: #19, #23, #41, #43, #14, #8, #9, #12, #15, #58, #60, native containment, recovery, migrated positive fixtures, full regression and exact-source CI. Requirements9 is unchanged. The unapproved #19 Design35 at 0993d2e is context only.

My Design10 Lows are addressed on the #43 side:
- the duplicate lookup's identity columns are body-derived, and a separate guard refuses binding if any non-indexable Session exists in scope (NULL cannot prove absence);
- the first binder requires the exact original marker W/body with zero preceding links;
- managed W writers are dedicated versioned UPDATEs, with no UPSERT or REPLACE and a full writer inventory;
- the diagnostic uses the same outside-lock sealed plan;
- hold clearance is its own reserved gate_hold link.
The #19 Design35 text at 0993d2e still folds clearance into the claim/observed projection. Aligning the joint projection goldens therefore remains a mandatory co-integration requirement.

The source slice is correct for its stated scope:
- PreparedInputAdmission is a new implementation-owned variant that no in-tree adapter advertises.
- step runs the preflight after the source and policy drift branches and before clear_hold, prepare_pack, reserve and the marker.
- EvidencePort phases skip it.
- The static role and admission check runs before probe.
- The probe identity (agent equal to the registered name, non-empty provider) and the probed role and admission capabilities are then enforced.
- The selected Arc, agent and provider are retained through preparation.
- The former post-reservation fail() paths for a missing reviewer, an unregistered agent or a missing capability are replaced by refusals with no writes.
- Claim, binding and owner rechecks are preserved.

The three negative tests compare complete Project/Goal/Task/Workflow/context/Session/lock/audit state, including an existing hold. They cover repeated refusal with zero probes and launches, missing, unregistered and wrong-role reviewers, and the six contradictory probe cases. The five recorded mutants each plausibly reach their intended consumer.

As honestly declared, the branch's legacy positive Workflow suite fails until a genuine #19 fixture migration. The earlier adapter ownership_change_during_native_preflight test failure (StateConflict expected, SessionLost observed) is outside this slice. Adapter.rs changes only the enum, and the cause is unmeasured. It must be diagnosed before full CI rather than rerun away.

Three Lows remain:
- an explicit staged fail-closed refusal is needed so advertising cannot reach legacy binding before the binder composes;
- the returned-identity and changed-selection checks are unexercised and must be labelled as such;
- the synchronous probe has no bounded-time contract.
There is no Critical, High or Medium finding in the staged component.

findings.claim:
The preflight selection is turned from an Option into a value with `?` only after the reservation has committed and the PreparationClaim has been created. If that `?` ever returned Err, `step` would exit before the `match result { Err(error) if eligible => release_preparation(..) }` handling. A committed native reservation would then be stranded without its owner-local #41 release.

The path is unreachable today, because `selected` is Some exactly when the actor is not EvidencePort and the preflight returns early on error. Its safety therefore rests on control-flow coupling, not on the types.
findings.evidence:
`self.reserve(&mut snapshot, &context, phase)?;` and `let claim = PreparationClaim::committed(&snapshot, index);` run first. Then `.prepare_agent(snapshot, AgentPreparation { ..., selected: selected.context("native phase requires preflight selection")?, }, &claim, &mut eligible)`.

The preflight_after_reservation mutant artifact shows the same shape of hazard: an Err after reserve leaves durable reservation state behind.
findings.fix: Resolve the native selection to a non-optional value before `reserve`. One way: a native branch that carries a `NativeAdapterSelection`, with EvidencePort taking a separate branch. If an absence check is kept, place it before reservation so no post-commit `?` sits outside the eligible/release accounting.

findings.claim: Capability, role and identity refusals are untyped `anyhow` strings produced by `ensure!`. A missing or unregistered adapter, by contrast, surfaces as a typed AdapterError (InvalidConfiguration). The design requires future scheduler, Goal and CLI integrations to recognise this pre-reservation configuration refusal and avoid hot retries. They cannot do that reliably without matching on strings, and the new tests themselves classify outcomes with `error.to_string().contains(..)`.
findings.evidence:
`ensure!(capabilities.contains(&required), "agent {agent} lacks prepared native phase capability {required:?}")`
`ensure!(info.agent == *agent && ..., "selected adapter probe identity mismatch")`
Design: 'Scheduler/Goal/CLI integrations must surface bounded configuration errors from pre-reservation Err and avoid hot retries'.
findings.fix: Return a typed, downcastable refusal (for example a `NativePreflightRefusal { agent, reason }` with variants for missing capability, role, identity and probe) for every preflight refusal. Assert on the typed variant in the controls.

findings.claim:
`preflight_native_adapter` calls the synchronous `AgentAdapter::probe()` directly inside the async `step`. GenericCliAdapter::probe performs blocking filesystem work (`resolve_executable` walks PATH and canonicalizes paths), and future native probes may do more. This differs from the local idiom: the same function runs rule/config file IO through `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.

The effect is invisible today only because no adapter advertises the capability, so the static check refuses before any probe runs.
findings.evidence: `let info = adapter.probe()?;` is called inside `async fn step` without spawn_blocking. The same function uses `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || load_rules(&project_for_rules, runtime)).await??` for its own filesystem reads. GenericCliAdapter::probe calls `resolve_executable(&self.command[0])`.
findings.fix: Run the probe on a blocking worker, holding the selected `Arc<dyn AgentAdapter>` and not holding the Store. Bound its duration, or document that implementers' probe() must be non-blocking, before any real adapter advertises PreparedInputAdmission.

review.assessment:
Reviewed the staged Source1 preflight component only, delta 6a72105→f2773cc (source b39b727; artifact head f277 is byte-identical source), against approved Requirements9/Design10. The unapproved #19 Design35 (0993d2e) is treated as a proposal.

Outcome: approve the staged preflight component only. This does not approve whole-#43 readiness, native readiness or merge.

My Design10 Lows are closed on the #43 side:
- D10-L1: the dedicated private writer uses an exact versioned UPDATE, BEFORE INSERT guards reject REPLACE/UPSERT, a complete inventory of Workflow writers is required, and the diagnostic port now uses the same outside-lock plan.
- D10-L2: the first binder requires the exact marker Workflow version and body hash with zero preceding links.
- D10-L3: hold clearance is its own reserved gate_hold link. The public #19 Design35 text still says clearance fits 'within claim/observed projection'. That alignment is recorded as a required joint golden and remains open on the dependency side.

Source correctness verified:
- Ordering: the preflight runs after the source/policy drift branches and before clear_hold, prepare_pack, reserve and the marker. EvidencePort phases skip it.
- Static check first: both the role capability and PreparedInputAdmission must appear in capabilities() before probe() is called.
- Probe identity: the probe's agent must equal the registered name and its provider must be nonempty. The probed capabilities must also include the role capability and PreparedInputAdmission.
- Retained selection: the same Arc, agent and probed provider are carried into prepare_agent. The existing reserved-actor/binding check still runs, plus a selection check whose failure goes through the eligible owner-local release rather than fail().
- Returned Session: provider and Task worktree are cross-checked (the extra worktree check is redundant but harmless).
- Removed post-reservation fail() paths: missing reviewer, unregistered adapter and unsupported capability now refuse before reservation with no durable write, as the design intends.
- Concurrent Task actor edits between preflight and reserve are caught by the reserve CAS.

Controls and mutations:
- The three controls exercise the real step and helper.
- The held-state test proves unchanged owners, Workflow, context, Sessions, locks and audit, zero launches, zero probes, and no new pack (exactly one capture per refusal).
- All six contradictory-probe cases reach distinct checks.
- The five compiled mutants each fail at the intended real consumer, and the restored source passes.
- No fixture advertises positive authority, and the spoofed descriptors are negative-only.

Declared limits, all honest and unwaived:
- The original legacy positive all_presets fixture fails on the missing PreparedInputAdmission capability. Full regression/CI cannot qualify until genuine #19 fixture migration.
- In this slice, fail-closed behaviour depends only on no in-tree adapter advertising the public enum variant. The real misadvertiser guard (the private binder plus the #19 allocation/input-pair proof) does not exist yet, so the branch must not merge or ship.
- Native provider-string equality between probe and Session for Claude/Codex/Grok must be verified at co-integration.
- The retained exploratory adapter failure (expected StateConflict, got SessionLost) is in code this delta touches only by adding an enum variant. Running that exact test at the pre-delta baseline would establish attribution without a flake rerun.

All mandatory gates stay open:
- the actual #19/#23/#41/#43/#14/#8/#9/#12/#15/#58/#60 producers and dedicated writers/guards, delivered in a single combined co-integration PR;
- fresh/migrated DDL goldens;
- the negative-index and non-indexable-scope controls;
- native 5/6/7 conformance and containment;
- restart recovery;
- the full mutation matrix;
- exact-head CI;
- independent source and security review.

This review covers only the supplied public bytes.
